output.reason: 45-year-old man with 30 minutes of ongoing crushing central chest pressure radiating to the left arm, with diaphoresis and nausea, on a background of high cholesterol. This pattern is sufficiently plausible for acute coronary syndrome to require immediate emergency assessment with ECG and troponin; no remote pathway can safely evaluate or treat this now.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now and stay resting until help arrives; do not drive yourself. Ongoing crushing chest pressure spreading to your left arm with sweating and nausea can signal a heart attack and needs emergency testing and treatment immediately. If you pass out or stop breathing, whoever is with you should tell the dispatcher right away and follow their instructions.
differential: Acute coronary syndrome (STEMI/NSTEMI or unstable angina) given pressure-type pain >20 minutes with left arm radiation, diaphoresis and nausea
Aortic dissection — pain character not described as tearing, but not excluded on reported information
Pulmonary embolism or other serious non-cardiac chest pain cause; no dyspnea or pleuritic features reported either way
